FIND: `_compute_cid()` does not hash packet content; it hashes only layer, name, text length, and model. Location:

```python
def _compute_cid(packets: list[DirectivePacket], model: str) -> str:
    """Compute a deterministic composition identity hash."""
    components = [
        f"{p.layer}:{p.name}:{len(p.text)}" for p in packets
    ]
    components.append(f"model:{model}")
    raw = "|".join(components)
    return hashlib.sha256(raw.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
```

Two directive sets with different text but the same packet layer/name/text length produce the same CID.

If distinct directive contents collide whenever packet names and lengths match, downstream logs, experiment analysis, and reproducibility checks can attribute behaviour to the wrong composed directive set. This is not merely a cryptographic collision risk; it is a deterministic aliasing bug caused by omitting the content from the hash input.
